sentences.text: Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili  HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE ABHINAND KUMAR SHAVILI  AND  HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE LAXMI NARAYANA ALISHETTY  WRIT APPEAL NO.1147 OF 2024 JUDGMENT:
(per Hon'ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty)
This Writ Appeal is filed aggrieved by the order dated 10.11.2023 passed by the learned single Judge of this Court in W.P.No.1663 of 2021.

2. Heard Sri Mukram Khan, learned counsel for appellant, learned Government Pleader for Services-I appearing for respondent nos.1 and 3 and Sri M.V.Rama Rao, learned standing counsel for respondent no.2.
3.

The facts of the case in nutshell are that in response to the notification dated 31.05.2018 issued by the 2nd respondent, appellant has applied for the post of Stipendiary Cadet Trainee Police Constable (for short, 'SCT PC') (Civil/etc.,) and was provisionally selected for the post of PCT PC (AR) subject to verification of the antecedents, original certificates and medical fitness; that during the antecedents verification, it came to light that he was involved in a AKS,J & LNA,J criminal case in Crime No.220/2018 under Sections 417 and 376(1) of IPC of Saroornagar Police Station, which was also mentioned in the attestation form during recruitment process; that appellant was served with show-cause notice on 19.02.2020 calling for his explanation as to why his provisional selection should not be cancelled in view of involvement in a serious case of moral turpitude; that appellant submitted his explanation dated 10.03.2020 stating that he fell in love with Kumari Nirmala and moved very closely and wanted to marry her after getting a government job and for the said reason,
he stopped meeting her, which promoted her to lodge a complaint against him in Saroornagar P.S.
with false and baseless allegations.

4. On knowing that a criminal case has been filed against him, he approached the victim girl,
explained the consequences faced by him in getting a government job and married her in Arya Samaj, Warasiguda, Secunderabad on 16.04.2018 and thereafter, they went to Police station and informed the same and filed a petition for quashing the case; that after recording her 164 Cr.P.C.
statement, the Police submitted final report dated 03.04.2018 dropping further action.
Basing on the said final report, the competent Court vide AKS,J & LNA,J order dated 06.10.2020 dropped the criminal proceedings as action dropped.

sentences.text: However, as per the report of the Superintendent of Police, Nagarkurnool District, vide letter dated 08.10.2020, it was stated that the appellant and the victim girl were living separately and the victim girl was married to another person; that the appellant did not furnish the true facts in his explanation and thus, cheated the victim girl.

Basing on the report of the Superintendent of Police,
dated 08.10.2020, the 2nd respondent cancelled the provisional selection of the appellant vide memo dated 22.10.2020.
6.

Aggrieved by the cancellation proceedings dated 22.10.2020, the appellant approached this Court by filing W.P.No.20210 of 2020 and this Court, vide order dated 16.11.2020, was pleased to allow the said writ petition with a direction to the respondents to examine the case of the appellant in terms of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Avtar Singh vs. Union of India and others 1 and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law.

entities.text: Avtar Singh vs. Union of India and others 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (2016) 8 SCC 471 AKS,J & LNA,J 7.
Appellant submitted representation to the 2nd respondent to consider his case by relying on the decision of this Court in W.P.No.20210 of 2020.

The 2nd respondent considered the case of the appellant and once again rejected the request of the appellant to appoint him as SCT PC vide Memo dated 28.12.2020 by observing that a candidate wishing to join Police Force must be a person of utmost rectitude and must have impeccable character and integrity and since the appellant has criminal antecedents, he is not fit for that job.

8. Aggrieved by the order dated 28.12.2020 passed by the 2nd respondent, appellant once again approached this Court by filing W.P.No.1663 of 2021 and the learned single Judge dismissed the said writ petition vide order dated 10.11.2023 by relying upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Union of India v. Methu Meda 2.
9.

entities.text: Union of India v. Methu Meda
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for appellant had contended that learned Single Judge erroneously dismissed writ petition of the appellant without taking into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Avatar Singh's case (1 supra).

Learned counsel (2022) 1 SCC 1 AKS,J & LNA,J further contended that despite specific orders passed by this Court in W.P.No.20210 of 2020 to consider the case of the appellant in terms of the guidelines laid down in Avatar Singh's case, the disciplinary authority cancelled the provisional selection in clear contravention of the ratio laid down and guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Avatar Singh's case.

Learned counsel further contended that despite a clean acquittal of appellant in criminal case, the disciplinary authority as well as learned single Judge did not consider the case in a proper perspective and therefore, the impugned order deserved interference by this Court.
10.

Per contra, learned standing counsel for respondents had contended that appellant was involved in a serious case of moral turpitude and in view of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Methu Meda (2 supra), the case of the appellant cannot be considered in view of his involvement in moral turpitude.
Learned Standing Counsel further contended that acquittal is not a clean acquittal and the case was dropped since the complainant did not intend to proceed with the criminal case.

AKS,J & LNA,J Edla Ganesh vs The State Of Telangana on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131212901/
2 11.

entities.text: Edla Ganesh vs The State Of Telangana on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned standing counsel further contended that from the record, it is revealed that appellant married the victim girl in Arya Samaj only to facilitate dropping of the case and it is further revealed that both are living separately and the victim girl was married to another person, which clearly shows that intention and conduct of the appellant in marrying the victim in Arya Samaj.

Therefore,
appellant is not fit person to be appointed in a disciplined force and finally, contended that no grounds are made out to interfere with the impugned order and the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

12. Perusal of the record would show that appellant is involved in a serious offence under Sections 417 and 376(1) of IPC and it is further revealed that the appellant married the victim girl in Arya Samaj and basing on the 164 Cr.P.C. statement of the victim girl, Police filed final report dropping the criminal case.

However, as per the proceedings dated 28.12.2020, by which the provisional selection of the appellant was cancelled, it revealed that appellant abandoned the victim girl and both are living separately and further the victim girl married to another person.
AKS,J & LNA,J 13.

It is relevant to refer to the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in State of Madhya Pradesh and others v. Bunty 3, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held that acquittal in a criminal case is based on the benefit of doubt or any other technical reason, the employer can take into consideration all relevant facts to take an appropriate decision as to the fitness of an incumbent for appointment/
continuance in service.
14.

entities.text: State of Madhya Pradesh and others v. Bunty 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Methu Meda (2 supra), the Hon'ble Apex Court held that if a person is acquitted by extending benefit of doubt from the charge of an offence involving moral turpitude or because the witnesses turned hostile, it would not automatically entitled him for employment, that too in disciplined forces.

15. In the present case, acquittal of the appellant in criminal case registered against him was not a clean acquittal and the case registered against him was dropped since he married the victim girl and she did not intend to prosecute the case and thus, the case was dropped against him.

Thereafter,
appellant abandoned the victim girl and it is also informed that the victim girl married another (2020) 17 SCC 654 AKS,J & LNA,J person, which infers that appellant married the girl in Arya Samaj only to get the criminal case closed.
Therefore, the disciplinary authority, duly taking into consideration of all the factual aspects, has passed orders dated 28.12.2020 rejecting the request of the appellant.

16. In the light of above discussion, legal position and involvement of the appellant in serious offence of moral turpitude, this Court does not find any illegality or irregularity in the order passed by the learned Single Judge.
Therefore, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the impugned order.
Writ Appeal fails and same is liable to be dismissed.
17. Accordingly, Writ Appeal is dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
